script.base: Working hypothesis from team form only: a competitive game with LA's passing offense offering the clearer route to sustained production, rather than either team establishing a large early lead. LA continues featuring D.Adams while sharing rushing work between K.Williams and B.Corum; PHI faces a less explosive offensive path against LA's defense. script.flip1: PHI's blitz disrupts LA and produces a PHI lead: LA's supplied QB EPA/dropback falls from 0.22 without a blitz to -0.23 against one. PHI can then increase rushing volume, threatening a S.Barkley combined-yardage under.
script.flip2: LA's passing efficiency produces an early multi-score lead, followed by a run-heavy second half. That could strand an Adams receiving over despite a favorable initial matchup, while forcing PHI toward passing.

pre_mortem: Adams: It is Monday and the over lost because PHI's blitz exploited LA's documented negative blitz EPA, or an early LA lead removed second-half passing volume. His three-game production may also conceal a long-play-heavy distribution; game logs and coverage assignments are absent. Barkley: The under lost because PHI controlled possession and concentrated carries in Barkley rather than maintaining the observed split, or his six receiving yards represented an unusually low stretch rather than a stable role. LA's aggregate rushing defense cannot rule out an individual explosive run. Both counter-cases cap confidence at lean.
slip_story: Both candidates fit a competitive, LA-pass-led game in which Adams remains the focal receiver and PHI never develops clock-killing Barkley volume. Adams can also survive PHI leading if protection holds; Barkley's under can survive LA leading if receiving usage stays limited. No forced parlay: two candidates do not justify inventing additional legs to reach a 3–4-leg main slip, and joint probabilities are unavailable.
